lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You look down... and see two Jacks.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Pocket Jacks. A great hand... and one of the easiest hands to lose a fortune with. Because how you play them depends on who is sitting across from you.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: So let's play the same hand against three very different players.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: What would you do?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Opponent one. The Rock. He has played two hands in the last hour. When he puts money in, he has it.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You raise to six dollars... and The Rock re-raises to twenty.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Call. His range is queens, kings, aces, or ace-king, so you are behind. Never four-bet into that. But you are deep, so you call, and see a flop.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: King, eight, three. And he bets twenty-eight.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Fold. He only bets here with ace-king, kings, or aces. Your jacks are crushed. Lay them down.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: He shows ace-king. That fold just saved your stack.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Lesson one. Against a rock, respect the raise.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Opponent two. The Maniac. He has raised every single hand tonight. Twice without even looking at his cards.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: The Maniac raises to eight. It's on you.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Three-bet. Against his huge range, jacks are a monster. Make him pay to play. You raise to twenty-six, and he calls.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Queen, seven, two. You bet twenty... and he instantly raises to sixty-five.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Just call. He would do this with any two cards. Don't scare him away. Let him keep bluffing.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: The four. And he shoves... all in.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Snap call. Against his range, your jacks are miles ahead.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Nine-eight. Total air. Your jacks hold, and you double up.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Lesson two. Against a maniac, let him hang himself.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Opponent three. The Calling Station. He never folds. Any pair, any draw, any reason at all.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You raise to six. He calls. Of course he does.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Eight, six, three. He checks to you.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Bet. Never slow-play against someone who calls everything. You bet ten. He calls.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: The deuce. He checks again.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Bet bigger. He is calling with any eight or six, and you beat all of those. Twenty-four. Called.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: And the river... a jack. You just made a set.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Go big. He can't fold top pair, and you have a set. Sixty dollars. He calls instantly.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Nine-eight. Top pair. You scoop a monster pot.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Lesson three. Against a calling station, never bluff. Just bet... and bet... and bet.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Same hand. Three opponents. Three completely different plays. Which ones did you get right? Tell me in the comments.
